import sqlite3
import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Reconnect to the database since it was closed earlier
conn = sqlite3.connect('lever.db')

# First, let's check if there are any tables at all
query = "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table';"
tables = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)

if len(tables) == 0:
    print("No tables found in the database. Checking for views...")
    query = "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='view';"
    views = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    print(f"Available views: {views}")
    
    if len(views) > 0:
        # Let's examine the first view
        first_view = views['name'].iloc[0]
        print(f"\nExamining view '{first_view}':")
        query = f"SELECT * FROM {first_view} LIMIT 5"
        sample_data = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
        print(f"Sample data from view '{first_view}':")
        print(sample_data)
        
        # Get column info for this view
        print(f"\nColumn information for view '{first_view}':")
        print(sample_data.dtypes)
        print(f"\nShape: {sample_data.shape}")
else:
    # If tables exist, examine the first one
    first_table = tables['name'].iloc[0]
    print(f"Examining table '{first_table}':")
    
    # Get sample data
    query = f"SELECT * FROM {first_table} LIMIT 10"
    sample_data = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    print(f"Sample data from table '{first_table}':")
    print(sample_data)
    
    # Get full data for analysis
    query = f"SELECT * FROM {first_table}"
    df = pd.read_sql_query(query, conn)
    
    # Basic data quality analysis
    print(f"\n=== Data Quality Analysis for '{first_table}' ===")
    print(f"Shape: {df.shape}")
    print(f"\nColumn Types:")
    print(df.dtypes)
    
    # Missing values analysis
    print(f"\nMissing Values:")
    missing = df.isnull().sum()
    missing_pct = (missing / len(df)) * 100
    missing_df = pd.DataFrame({
        'Missing Count': missing,
        'Missing %': missing_pct
    })
    print(missing_df[missing_df['Missing Count'] > 0])
    
    # Identify text columns that might contain notes or remarks
    text_columns = df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns
    print(f"\nText columns (potential for notes/remarks): {list(text_columns)}")
    
    # Check for columns with "note", "remark", "comment" in their names
    note_columns = [col for col in df.columns if any(keyword in col.lower() 
                   for keyword in ['note', 'remark', 'comment', 'description', 'text'])]
    print(f"\nColumns likely containing notes/remarks: {note_columns}")
    
    if note_columns:
        print(f"\nSample content from note columns:")
        for col in note_columns[:3]:  # Limit to first 3 note columns
            if col in df.columns:
                non_null_notes = df[col].dropna()
                if len(non_null_notes) > 0:
                    print(f"\n{col} (first 3 non-null values):")
                    for note in non_null_notes.head(3):
                        print(f"  - {str(note)[:100]}...")
    
    # Analyze numeric columns
    numeric_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=[np.number]).columns
    if len(numeric_cols) > 0:
        print(f"\n=== Numeric Columns Analysis ===")
        print(f"Numeric columns: {list(numeric_cols)}")
        
        # Basic statistics
        print(f"\nDescriptive statistics:")
        print(df[numeric_cols].describe())
        
        # Check for outliers using IQR method
        print(f"\nPotential outliers (using IQR method):")
        for col in numeric_cols:
            Q1 = df[col].quantile(0.25)
            Q3 = df[col].quantile(0.75)
            IQR = Q3 - Q1
            lower_bound = Q1 - 1.5 * IQR
            upper_bound = Q3 + 1.5 * IQR
            outliers = df[(df[col] < lower_bound) | (df[col] > upper_bound)][col]
            if len(outliers) > 0:
                print(f"{col}: {len(outliers)} outliers ({len(outliers)/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")
    
    # Analyze categorical/text columns
    categorical_cols = df.select_dtypes(include=['object']).columns
    if len(categorical_cols) > 0:
        print(f"\n=== Categorical/Text Columns Analysis ===")
        for col in categorical_cols[:5]:  # Limit to first 5 columns
            unique_count = df[col].nunique()
            print(f"\n{col}:")
            print(f"  Unique values: {unique_count}")
            print(f"  Missing values: {df[col].isnull().sum()} ({df[col].isnull().sum()/len(df)*100:.1f}%)")
            
            if unique_count <= 10:  # Show value counts for low-cardinality columns
                print(f"  Value distribution:")
                print(df[col].value_counts(dropna=False).head())

conn.close()
